newsitem.title: GERMANY: German media disappointed over tax talk failure.
newsitem.headline: German media disappointed over tax talk failure.

text.p: German media commentators voiced deep disappointment on Thursday at the failure of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition and opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to reach agreement on tax reform.

The popular tabloid Bild Zeitung pondered whether the collapse of talks on Wednesday would put the planned 30 billion mark tax cuts in jeopardy, and accused German leaders of preening for the media in an extended prelude to the 1998 elections.
"Will the tax cut be the next to fail?" Bild asked in a front-page headline.
"This is not politics. It is a circus. A third-rate circus," a Bild editorial said.

"With over four million unemployed in Germany, and gigantic gaps in state finances...our politicians could not sit together for more than 55 minutes before running from each other, in the direction of the cameras and microphones," it said.
The tax reform was portrayed by both sides as badly needed to stimulate investment and jobs creation in the face of record unemployment.

The collapse of the talks means Kohl and Finance Minister Theo Waigel will have to push the tax legislation through parliament via the usual channels, risking a blockade by the SPD, which holds the majority in the upper house.
The confrontation is bound to repeat itself in parliament's mediation committee next autumn.

The sober Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung said: "In hindsight, one has to wonder about the high expectations that were invested in the attempt to reach an agreement via informal routes that were already crackling in the glare of media speculation ahead of anticipation of (next year's) elections."
Future efforts to put the tax cuts back on track will have to fight a headwind of sloganeering about financing, value-added taxes and Maastricht, the business daily said.

The Sueddeutsche Zeitung, in a play on the words of German poet Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, said, "Over all tax summits is calm, in all treetops you will find, barely a whiff of reform." -- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-2609750
